Article summary When shopping for a lab-grown diamond, you've likely come across the terms CVD and HPHT. While these manufacturing methods sound technical, they simply describe how a diamond is grown in a laboratory. Both methods produce real diamonds with the same brilliance, durability, and beauty as natural diamonds, but they differ in their growth process and certain characteristics. In this guide, we'll explain CVD and HPHT in simple terms, compare their differences, debunk common myths, and help you understand what truly matters when choosing a certified lab-grown diamond. As lab-grown diamonds continue to grow in popularity, buyers are becoming more interested in understanding how these remarkable gemstones are created. During your research, you've probably encountered two technical terms: CVD (Chemical Vapour Deposition) and HPHT (High Pressure High Temperature) . At first glance, these names can seem confusing and may even make it feel like one type of diamond is better than the other. In reality, both CVD and HPHT are simply different methods of growing genuine diamonds inside a laboratory. Both produce real diamonds with identical chemical composition, hardness, brilliance, and durability. Once they are cut, polished, and certified, even experienced jewellers cannot distinguish between them with the naked eye. This guide explains how each process works, the key differences between them, and what you should actually focus on when buying a certified lab-grown diamond. What Are Lab-Grown Diamonds? Before comparing CVD and HPHT, it's important to understand what a lab-grown diamond actually is. A lab-grown diamond is a genuine diamond made from pure carbon atoms arranged in the same crystal structure as a natural diamond. Instead of forming beneath the Earth's surface over billions of years, these diamonds are grown inside highly controlled laboratories using advanced scientific processes. Because they share the same physical, chemical, and optical properties as natural diamonds, lab-grown diamonds offer the same brilliance, fire, hardness, and durability. They are also graded using the same internationally recognised standards based on the 4Cs—Cut, Colour, Clarity, and Carat Weight. Whether a diamond is grown using CVD or HPHT, it remains a real diamond. The method used to grow a diamond does not determine whether it is real. Both CVD and HPHT produce genuine diamonds. What Is HPHT? HPHT stands for High Pressure High Temperature , and it is the oldest commercial method used to create lab-grown diamonds. This process recreates the extreme conditions found deep beneath the Earth's surface, where natural diamonds are formed. Scientists place a tiny diamond seed inside a specialised growth chamber along with pure carbon. The chamber then applies enormous pressure and extremely high temperatures, allowing carbon atoms to crystallise around the seed and gradually form a new diamond. The HPHT process closely mimics the natural environment in which Earth-grown diamonds develop, making it one of the most trusted methods of diamond production. How HPHT Works 1. A small diamond seed is placed inside a high-pressure chamber. 2. Pure carbon is introduced around the seed. 3. The chamber generates extreme heat and pressure. 4. Carbon atoms bond to the seed crystal. 5. Over several weeks, a rough diamond is formed. 6. The rough diamond is then cut, polished, and certified. CVD stands for Chemical Vapour Deposition , one of the most advanced and widely used technologies for growing gem-quality lab-grown diamonds today. Instead of using extreme pressure, CVD grows diamonds inside a specialised vacuum chamber filled with carbon-rich gases. These gases are heated until they become plasma, allowing carbon atoms to slowly attach themselves to a diamond seed one microscopic layer at a time. This controlled process allows manufacturers to carefully monitor the growth of each diamond, producing exceptional quality and consistency. Today, many premium jewellery brands use CVD diamonds because of their precision and ability to produce high-quality gemstones. How CVD Works 1. A thin diamond seed is placed inside a vacuum chamber. 2. Carbon-rich gases are introduced. 3. The gases are converted into plasma using energy. 4. Carbon atoms settle onto the seed. 5. The diamond grows layer by layer. 6. The rough diamond is cut, polished, and independently certified. Although CVD and HPHT use completely different technologies to grow diamonds, the finished product is remarkably similar. Once a diamond has been cut, polished, and graded, its beauty is determined by its quality rather than the manufacturing process. For buyers, the differences are usually invisible. The sparkle, brilliance, hardness, and durability remain the same because both diamonds are genuine carbon crystals. The biggest differences lie in the manufacturing techniques rather than in how the finished diamond performs. CVD Diamonds Grown using carbon-rich gas. Built layer by layer. Highly controlled manufacturing process. Widely used for premium jewellery. Produces excellent gem-quality diamonds. HPHT Diamonds Created using extreme pressure and heat. Mimics Earth's natural diamond formation. One of the oldest commercial growth methods. Produces genuine gem-quality diamonds. Commonly used around the world. Does One Sparkle More Than the Other? One of the biggest myths surrounding lab-grown diamonds is that one manufacturing method produces more sparkle than the other. This simply isn't true. A diamond's sparkle depends primarily on its cut quality , not whether it was grown using CVD or HPHT. An Excellent-cut CVD diamond will sparkle beautifully. Likewise, an Excellent-cut HPHT diamond will display the same fire and brilliance. Rather than asking which process creates a "better" diamond, buyers should focus on choosing the best cut grade possible. The cut of a diamond influences its sparkle far more than the technology used to grow it. What Should You Look for Instead? Instead of concentrating solely on whether a diamond was grown using CVD or HPHT, focus on the factors that genuinely affect beauty and long-term satisfaction. Choose a diamond with an independent certification, excellent cut quality, eye-clean clarity, attractive colour, and craftsmanship you can trust. These characteristics will have a far greater impact on your experience than the manufacturing process. Buying from a reputable jeweller who provides complete transparency and certification is far more important than choosing one growth method over another. Always check: Independent diamond certification Excellent cut grade Colour and clarity Carat weight Secure ring setting Trusted jeweller Warranty and after-sales support Final Thoughts CVD and HPHT are simply two different paths to creating the same remarkable result—a genuine lab-grown diamond. While the science behind each process is fascinating, it shouldn't be the deciding factor in your purchase. The qualities that truly matter are the diamond's cut, certification, craftsmanship, and how well it matches your personal style and budget. At House of Diams, we carefully select certified lab-grown diamonds based on their beauty and quality rather than the technology used to grow them. Every diamond is chosen to meet the highest standards so you can shop with complete confidence. Whether you choose a CVD or HPHT diamond, you're investing in a timeless piece of jewellery designed to celebrate life's most meaningful moments. The best diamond isn't defined by how it was grown—it's defined by the joy it brings every time you wear it. Article summary Choosing between a lab-grown diamond and a natural diamond is one of the biggest decisions you'll make when shopping for an engagement ring or fine jewellery. Both are real diamonds with exceptional beauty, but they differ in origin, price, rarity, and long-term value. This guide provides an honest comparison to help you confidently choose the option that best suits your lifestyle, budget, and personal preferences. Buying a diamond is one of life's most meaningful purchases, whether you're choosing an engagement ring, celebrating an anniversary, or investing in a timeless piece of fine jewellery. Today, buyers have more choices than ever before, with both lab-grown and natural diamonds offering remarkable beauty and durability. One of the most common questions we hear at House of Diams is, "Should I choose a lab-grown diamond or a natural diamond?" The answer isn't about which option is better—it depends on what matters most to you. Both are genuine diamonds. Both sparkle beautifully. Both can last a lifetime. Yet they differ in how they are created, their rarity, their price, and the reasons people choose them. In this guide, we'll compare lab-grown and natural diamonds honestly, helping you understand the differences so you can make a confident and informed decision. A lab-grown diamond is a real diamond that is created inside a controlled laboratory using advanced technology. Scientists recreate the same conditions under which diamonds naturally form beneath the Earth's surface, allowing pure carbon atoms to grow into a genuine diamond crystal. Because the crystal structure is identical, a lab-grown diamond has the same hardness, brilliance, fire, and durability as a mined diamond. Even professional jewellers cannot distinguish between them with the naked eye. Only specialized laboratory equipment can identify how a diamond was formed. Lab-grown diamonds are certified by respected gemological laboratories, including IGI, and graded using the same internationally recognized standards as natural diamonds. A lab-grown diamond is not a diamond imitation—it is a genuine diamond with the same physical, chemical, and optical properties as a natural diamond. What Is a Natural Diamond? Natural diamonds are formed deep within the Earth's mantle under immense pressure and heat over billions of years. Volcanic activity gradually brings these diamonds closer to the Earth's surface, where they are eventually discovered and mined. Every natural diamond is unique because it has been shaped by geological processes over an incredibly long period. For many buyers, this natural origin carries emotional significance and a sense of rarity that cannot be replicated. Like lab-grown diamonds, natural diamonds are cut, polished, and graded according to the 4Cs: cut, colour, clarity, and carat weight. One of the biggest misconceptions about lab-grown diamonds is that they somehow "look different." In reality, they don't. Both lab-grown and natural diamonds have identical optical properties. They reflect light in the same way, produce the same sparkle, and display the same brilliance and fire. When placed side by side, even experienced jewellers cannot reliably identify which diamond is lab-grown without specialized equipment. For everyday wear, there is no visible difference between the two. This means your decision should be based on factors such as budget, origin, personal values, and long-term goals rather than appearance alone. Both diamonds offer: Exceptional brilliance The same Mohs hardness rating of 10 Excellent durability for everyday wear The same sparkle and fire Professional certification Lifetime wearability Price Comparison: Where Do You Get Better Value? Price is often the biggest deciding factor for many buyers. Lab-grown diamonds generally cost significantly less than natural diamonds of comparable size and quality. This allows buyers to choose a larger centre stone, higher clarity, or better colour grade while staying within the same budget. For example, instead of purchasing a smaller natural diamond, many couples can choose a larger certified lab-grown diamond without compromising on beauty or quality. Natural diamonds, on the other hand, command higher prices because they are rare, naturally formed over billions of years, and require mining and extensive supply chains before reaching the jewellery market. Ultimately, the better value depends on your priorities. If maximizing size and quality within your budget is important, lab-grown diamonds often provide exceptional value. If rarity and natural origin are your priorities, a natural diamond may feel more meaningful. The best diamond isn't the most expensive one—it's the one that aligns with your priorities, lifestyle, and budget. Durability: Which Diamond Lasts Longer? When investing in an engagement ring or fine jewellery, durability is just as important as beauty. Fortunately, this is one area where both lab-grown and natural diamonds perform equally well. Both diamonds rank 10 on the Mohs Hardness Scale , making them the hardest naturally occurring material known. This exceptional hardness means they are highly resistant to scratches and suitable for everyday wear. Whether you're wearing your engagement ring daily, travelling, working, or enjoying outdoor activities, both types of diamonds will maintain their sparkle for generations with proper care. Rather than focusing solely on whether a diamond is lab-grown or natural, buyers should pay close attention to the quality of the setting, the type of metal, and routine jewellery maintenance. What affects durability more than the diamond itself? Although the diamond itself is incredibly durable, the ring's overall longevity depends on several other factors. A secure setting, strong metal choice, and regular inspections help keep your diamond safe for years to come. Prongs can wear down over time, and rings worn every day naturally experience small amounts of wear. Having your jewellery professionally checked once or twice a year helps ensure your diamond remains secure. Independent gemological laboratories evaluate diamonds based on internationally recognised grading standards known as the 4Cs : Cut Colour Clarity Carat Weight These reports provide buyers with confidence by accurately documenting a diamond's quality and characteristics. For lab-grown diamonds, respected laboratories such as IGI (International Gemological Institute) clearly identify the diamond as laboratory-grown while grading it using the same standards applied to natural diamonds. Always ask to see the certificate before making your purchase and verify the report number through the laboratory's official website whenever possible. Certification gives buyers confidence because it independently verifies exactly what they are purchasing. Resale Value: What Should Buyers Expect? Many people ask whether diamonds are good financial investments. The honest answer is that jewellery should primarily be purchased for its emotional and personal value rather than as an investment. Natural diamonds have historically retained a portion of their value due to their rarity and established resale market. However, resale prices vary depending on market demand, brand, certification, and overall condition. Lab-grown diamonds are a newer category, and as production technology continues to improve, prices have become more affordable over time. Because of this, resale values for lab-grown diamonds are generally lower than those of comparable natural diamonds. If long-term investment potential is your primary concern, discussing your goals with a trusted jeweller before purchasing is always recommended. Things to remember about resale value: 1. Jewellery should be purchased primarily for personal enjoyment. 2. Certified diamonds generally have stronger resale potential. 3. Premium craftsmanship can increase long-term desirability. 4. Keep all original certificates and purchase documentation. 5. Buy the diamond you truly love rather than focusing solely on future resale. Ethical and Environmental Considerations Many buyers today also consider how their diamond was sourced. Lab-grown diamonds are created in laboratories without traditional mining, making them an attractive option for buyers who prefer a modern manufacturing process. Natural diamonds, on the other hand, support mining communities around the world and remain an important source of employment in many regions. Rather than assuming one option is universally "better," it's important to understand that every diamond has its own supply chain and environmental impact. Reputable jewellers should always be transparent about the origin of their diamonds and provide honest information so customers can make informed decisions. Transparency matters more than marketing claims. Choose a jeweller who openly shares information about the origin of every diamond. Article summary Choosing between 14K and 18K gold is just as important as choosing the perfect diamond. While both are excellent options for engagement rings and fine jewellery, they differ in durability, gold purity, colour, price, maintenance, and everyday wear. In this guide, we'll explain the key differences between 14K and 18K gold, compare their advantages and disadvantages, and help you decide which one best suits your lifestyle, budget, and jewellery preferences. When shopping for an engagement ring or fine jewellery, most people spend hours choosing the perfect diamond—but often overlook the metal that holds it. The type of gold you choose plays a significant role in the ring's appearance, durability, maintenance, and long-term value. Two of the most popular choices are 14K gold and 18K gold . While they may look similar at first glance, they differ in gold purity, strength, colour, and price. Neither option is universally better. The right choice depends on how you plan to wear your jewellery, your budget, and the look you want to achieve. In this guide, we'll compare 14K and 18K gold in detail, helping you choose the best option for your engagement ring or fine jewellery. What Do 14K and 18K Gold Mean? Pure gold is naturally soft, making it unsuitable for everyday jewellery on its own. To improve durability, jewellers mix pure gold with other metals such as silver, copper, zinc, or palladium. The term karat (K) refers to the amount of pure gold contained in the alloy. The higher the karat, the greater the percentage of pure gold. 24K Gold – 99.9% pure gold. 18K Gold – 75% pure gold and 25% alloy metals. 14K Gold – 58.5% pure gold and 41.5% alloy metals. Because both 14K and 18K contain additional metals, they are much stronger than pure 24K gold and are ideal for engagement rings that are worn every day. The difference isn't about quality—it's about finding the right balance between purity, durability, and lifestyle. Appearance: Can You Tell the Difference? One of the first things buyers notice is colour. Since 18K gold contains a higher percentage of pure gold, it has a richer, warmer yellow tone. The colour appears slightly deeper and more luxurious. 14K gold contains more alloy metals, giving it a slightly lighter yellow appearance. For many people, the difference is subtle and often difficult to notice without comparing the two rings side by side. If you're choosing white gold, the colour difference becomes even less noticeable because both 14K and 18K white gold are typically finished with rhodium plating. If you wear your engagement ring every day, durability should be one of your biggest considerations. Because 14K gold contains more alloy metals, it is naturally harder and more resistant to scratches, dents, and everyday wear. 18K gold, while still highly durable, is slightly softer because of its higher gold content. This doesn't mean 18K is fragile—it simply requires a little more care over time. For people with active lifestyles or hands-on professions, 14K gold is often considered the more practical option. Choose 14K Gold if you: Wear your ring every day. Have an active lifestyle. Work with your hands. Want extra scratch resistance. Prefer lower maintenance. Choose 18K Gold if you: Prefer richer gold colour. Appreciate higher gold purity. Mostly wear jewellery on special occasions. Want a more luxurious appearance. Price Comparison Gold purity directly affects price. Because 18K gold contains more pure gold, it costs more than 14K gold. Choosing 14K gold can often free up part of your budget, allowing you to invest in a larger diamond, a higher clarity grade, or a more elaborate setting. If your overall budget is fixed, many buyers choose 14K gold and allocate the savings toward improving the diamond itself. Many buyers won't notice the difference between 14K and 18K—but they will notice a beautifully cut diamond. Which Gold Is Better for Sensitive Skin? People with sensitive skin often wonder whether one type of gold is more comfortable than the other. Because 18K gold contains a higher percentage of pure gold and fewer alloy metals, it may be a better choice for people with certain metal sensitivities. However, the exact composition of the alloy also matters, as different jewellers use different metal mixtures. If you have a known allergy, ask your jeweller about the specific alloy used before making your purchase. Maintenance and Long-Term Care Both 14K and 18K gold require occasional maintenance to keep them looking their best. Regular cleaning with warm water, mild soap, and a soft brush helps remove dirt and restore shine. Professional inspections are also recommended once or twice a year to ensure the prongs holding your diamond remain secure. Over time, every engagement ring develops small signs of wear, which is perfectly normal and part of its story. Proper care will keep either gold alloy looking beautiful for decades. If you're looking for maximum durability and value for everyday wear, 14K gold is an outstanding choice. It offers excellent strength, beautiful colour, and allows you to allocate more of your budget toward your diamond. If you appreciate richer gold colour, higher purity, and a more luxurious feel, 18K gold is an exceptional option that has long been associated with fine jewellery. Whichever you choose, remember that craftsmanship, diamond quality, and thoughtful design contribute just as much to the beauty of your engagement ring as the gold itself. A Complete Buyer’s Guide Article summary Everything you need to know about lab-grown diamonds, how they are made, and what to check before buying. Are Lab-Grown Diamonds Real? A Complete Buyer’s Guide Lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds. They are not imitations, not crystals that only look like diamonds, and not a compromise on beauty or durability. A lab-grown diamond has the same carbon structure, hardness, brilliance and fire as a diamond mined from the earth. The key difference is origin. Natural diamonds formed beneath the earth over billions of years, while lab-grown diamonds are created in a controlled environment using advanced technology that recreates the conditions needed for diamond growth. For many buyers, lab-grown diamonds offer the opportunity to choose a larger diamond, a higher-quality grade, or a more detailed jewellery design within the same budget. This guide explains what lab-grown diamonds are, how they are made, and what you should check before purchasing. How Are Lab-Grown Diamonds Made? Lab-grown diamonds are created from a small diamond seed using one of two advanced processes: High Pressure High Temperature, known as HPHT, or Chemical Vapour Deposition, known as CVD. HPHT Diamonds HPHT stands for High Pressure High Temperature. This method recreates the extreme heat and pressure found deep within the earth, allowing carbon to crystallise around a diamond seed. The result is a real diamond with the same core properties as a mined diamond. CVD Diamonds CVD stands for Chemical Vapour Deposition. In this process, a diamond seed is placed inside a controlled chamber filled with carbon-rich gas. The carbon gradually forms layers on the seed until a diamond crystal grows. Both CVD and HPHT methods produce genuine diamonds. After the diamond is grown, it is cut, polished and graded in the same way as a natural diamond. Lab-Grown Diamonds Are Not Simulants A lab-grown diamond is different from a diamond simulant. Diamond simulants, such as cubic zirconia and moissanite, may look similar to diamonds but are different materials with different chemical, physical and optical properties. A lab-grown diamond is a real diamond made from carbon. It has the same hardness and sparkle as a natural diamond. When buying online, always check whether the product description clearly says “lab-grown diamond” and not simply “created stone” or “diamond simulant.” Are Lab-Grown Diamonds Certified? Yes. Independent gemological laboratories can grade lab-grown diamonds using the same important standards used for natural diamonds: cut, colour, clarity and carat weight. These are known as the 4Cs. For important centre stones, buyers should ask for an independent grading report from a recognised laboratory, such as IGI. The report confirms that the diamond is laboratory-grown and records its individual characteristics. Before making a purchase, ask the jeweller if the report number can be verified directly with the grading laboratory. This adds confidence and helps you understand exactly what you are buying. What Should You Check Before Buying a Lab-Grown Diamond? Certification: Ask whether the centre diamond comes with an independent grading report. Cut quality: Cut has a major effect on brilliance and sparkle. A well-cut diamond can look brighter than a larger diamond with a poor cut. The 4Cs: Compare cut, colour, clarity and carat weight before choosing a stone. Metal and setting: Choose between 14K gold, 18K gold or platinum based on your style and everyday lifestyle. Ring size: Confirm the correct size before ordering, especially for international purchases. After-sales service: Review the brand’s resizing, warranty, returns and international shipping policies before payment. Choosing Your Lab-Grown Diamond Ring The right ring is personal. Some buyers prefer a larger carat size, while others prioritise exceptional cut quality, a colourless appearance, or a custom-designed setting. Popular choices include round brilliant, oval, emerald-cut, cushion-cut and pear-shaped lab-grown diamonds. Each shape has a different personality, sparkle pattern and appearance on the hand. We are here to help you choose a piece that feels personal, beautiful and made to be worn for years. “The best diamond is not simply the largest one. /blog/the-4cs-of-lab-grown-diamonds-expl.text: ← Back to Journal The 4Cs of Lab-Grown Diamonds Reading time 9 min read Published Aug 11, 2026 Written by House of Diams Jewellery Team The 4Cs of Lab-Grown Diamonds Explained: How to Choose the Perfect Diamond Article summary Buying a diamond becomes much easier once you understand the 4Cs—Cut, Colour, Clarity, and Carat Weight. These four grading factors determine a diamond's beauty, quality, and value, whether it's lab-grown or natural. In this guide, you'll learn what each of the 4Cs means, which one matters the most, where you should spend your budget, and how to choose a certified lab-grown diamond that offers the perfect balance of brilliance and value. Buying a diamond can feel overwhelming when you're faced with unfamiliar grading terms like Cut , Colour , Clarity , and Carat Weight . These four characteristics, commonly known as the 4Cs , are the global standard used to evaluate every diamond, whether it's mined from the earth or grown in a laboratory. Understanding the 4Cs empowers you to make a confident purchase rather than relying solely on price or appearance. Instead of simply choosing the biggest diamond within your budget, you'll know how to select a stone that delivers exceptional brilliance, beauty, and long-term value. In this guide, we'll break down each of the 4Cs in simple language, explain why some factors matter more than others, and share practical buying tips to help you choose the perfect certified lab-grown diamond. What Are the 4Cs of Diamonds? The 4Cs were developed as the universal diamond grading system to help buyers compare diamonds objectively. Every certified diamond is evaluated based on these four characteristics: Cut – How well the diamond reflects light. Colour – How colourless the diamond appears. Clarity – The presence of natural inclusions or blemishes. Carat Weight – The weight and perceived size of the diamond. These grading standards apply equally to both lab-grown and natural diamonds. Whether you're shopping for an engagement ring or a pair of diamond earrings, understanding the 4Cs is essential to making a smart purchase. The most beautiful diamond isn't always the biggest one—it's the one with the right balance of the 4Cs. 1. Cut – The Most Important of the 4Cs If there is one characteristic you should never compromise on, it's Cut . Many people mistakenly believe that cut refers to a diamond's shape, such as oval, round, or pear. In reality, cut measures how precisely a diamond has been crafted to reflect light. A well-cut diamond allows light to enter through the top, bounce around the internal facets, and return to your eye as brilliant sparkle. A poorly cut diamond allows light to escape through the sides or bottom, making it appear dull regardless of its size or clarity. This is why two diamonds with the same carat weight can look completely different in terms of brilliance. Cut Grades Excellent Very Good Good Fair Poor Whenever possible, choose a diamond with an Excellent or Very Good cut grade. The difference in sparkle is immediately noticeable and often has a greater visual impact than increasing carat weight or clarity. Colour – How White Is Your Diamond? Diamond colour measures how colourless a diamond appears. Contrary to what many people think, the highest-quality white diamonds actually have less colour , not more. The grading scale begins at D , which represents a completely colourless diamond, and continues through the alphabet as more warmth or yellow tint becomes visible. Most buyers won't notice the difference between neighbouring grades without specialised equipment, making it possible to achieve excellent value by choosing the right colour range. Diamond Colour Scale D–F: Colourless (highest grades) G–H: Near Colourless (excellent value) I–J: Slight warmth visible K and below: Noticeable colour tint For most engagement rings, G and H colour diamonds provide the ideal balance between beauty and value. They appear beautifully white once set while costing significantly less than D or E colour diamonds. If you're choosing a yellow gold setting, slightly warmer colour grades can still look stunning because the metal naturally complements the diamond. 3. Clarity – Understanding Nature's Fingerprints Clarity refers to the tiny natural characteristics found inside or on the surface of a diamond. These internal marks are called inclusions , while surface marks are known as blemishes . Almost every diamond contains these microscopic characteristics, making each one unique. Fortunately, most inclusions are invisible without magnification and have no effect on a diamond's beauty. Rather than paying significantly more for perfection that cannot be seen with the naked eye, many buyers prefer diamonds that appear "eye-clean." Common Clarity Grades FL – Flawless IF – Internally Flawless VVS1 & VVS2 – Very Very Slightly Included VS1 & VS2 – Very Slightly Included SI1 & SI2 – Slightly Included I1–I3 – Included For excellent value, many jewellery experts recommend choosing VS1 , VS2 , or an eye-clean SI1 diamond. These grades often appear identical to much higher clarity diamonds without the premium price tag. Carat Weight – Bigger Isn't Always Better Carat refers to a diamond's weight , not its physical size. One carat equals 0.20 grams , but two diamonds with the same carat weight can appear different in size depending on their shape and cut quality. Many buyers assume that increasing carat weight automatically creates a more beautiful diamond. However, a smaller diamond with an excellent cut often appears brighter and more attractive than a larger diamond with poor proportions. Understanding how carat weight influences pricing can also help you maximise your budget. Smart Buying Tip Diamond prices increase significantly at popular weight milestones such as 1.00 carat , 1.50 carats , and 2.00 carats . Instead of purchasing exactly one carat, consider diamonds weighing 0.90–0.95 carats . They often look almost identical in size while costing considerably less. The same strategy applies to larger diamonds, allowing you to maximise value without sacrificing appearance. A well-cut 0.90-carat diamond can outshine a poorly cut 1-carat diamond every single day. How Should You Prioritise the 4Cs? Every buyer has a different budget, but the best approach is to prioritise the characteristics that have the greatest impact on beauty. While all four grading factors are important, they don't contribute equally to a diamond's appearance. 1. Prioritise Cut above everything else. 2. Choose a carat weight that suits your budget. 3. Select a colour grade that appears white in your chosen metal. 4. Choose an eye-clean clarity grade instead of paying extra for microscopic perfection. The Ideal 4Cs for Most Buyers If you're looking for an exceptional balance of beauty, quality, and value, many jewellery professionals recommend the following combination: Excellent Cut G or H Colour VS1 or VS2 Clarity Carat Weight based on your budget This combination delivers outstanding brilliance while avoiding unnecessary costs for characteristics that are rarely visible to the naked eye. A perfectly fitted ring feels comfortable, stays secure, and makes your overall jewellery experience much more enjoyable. Whether you're shopping for yourself or planning a surprise proposal, this guide explains several easy ways to measure your ring size at home, understand international ring size conversions, avoid common sizing mistakes, and ensure you choose the perfect fit before placing your order. Buying a beautiful ring online is exciting, but choosing the wrong size can quickly turn that excitement into frustration. A ring that's too loose may slip off unexpectedly, while one that's too tight can become uncomfortable to wear every day. Fortunately, finding your correct ring size isn't as difficult as many people think. With a few simple tools and the right technique, you can accurately measure your ring size from the comfort of your home before placing your order. Whether you're purchasing an engagement ring, wedding band, anniversary gift, or a special piece for yourself, understanding ring sizing helps ensure your jewellery fits comfortably from the very first wear. In this guide, we'll show you several reliable methods to measure your ring size, explain international sizing systems, and share practical tips to help you avoid common sizing mistakes. Why Choosing the Correct Ring Size Matters A well-fitted ring should feel secure without feeling tight. It should slide comfortably over your knuckle with a slight amount of resistance and sit naturally at the base of your finger throughout the day. Wearing the correct size improves comfort, reduces the risk of losing your ring, and helps protect the setting from unnecessary stress caused by forcing a ring on or off your finger. When purchasing a valuable engagement ring or diamond jewellery, spending a few extra minutes measuring your finger correctly can save both time and future resizing costs. The perfect ring isn't just beautiful—it fits so naturally that you almost forget you're wearing it. Method 1: Measure an Existing Ring If you already own a ring that fits perfectly on the finger you're buying for, this is one of the easiest and most accurate methods. Place the ring on a flat surface and measure the inside diameter using a ruler with millimetre markings or a digital caliper. Make sure you're measuring from the inside edge of one side directly to the inside edge of the opposite side. Once you have the diameter, compare it with a reliable ring size chart to determine your correct size. 1. Choose a ring that fits comfortably. 2. Place it on a flat surface. 3. Measure the inside diameter in millimetres. 4. Compare the measurement with a ring size chart. 5. Double-check the measurement for accuracy. It should move over your knuckle with slight resistance but should not feel tight or uncomfortable. Repeat the measurement two or three times to ensure consistent results. Method 3: Measure with String or Paper If you don't have a ring or a sizing tool, a thin strip of paper or a non-stretch string can also help you estimate your size. Wrap the paper around the base of your finger, mark where the ends meet, and measure the length using a ruler. Compare the circumference measurement with an international ring size chart. /blog/igi-certification-for-lab-grown-di.text: ← Back to Journal IGI Certification for Lab-Grown Diamonds Reading time 9 min read Published Sep 30, 2026 Written by House of Diams Jewellery Team IGI Certification Explained: Everything You Need to Know Before Buying a Lab-Grown Diamond Article summary When buying a lab-grown diamond, one of the most important documents you'll receive is its certification. An independent grading report gives you confidence that the diamond has been professionally evaluated and accurately graded. But what exactly is IGI certification, what information does it include, and why should it matter to you? In this guide, we'll explain everything you need to know about IGI certification, how to read a grading report, how to verify its authenticity, and why certification plays such an important role when purchasing a lab-grown diamond engagement ring. Buying a diamond is a significant investment, and one of the best ways to protect that investment is by ensuring your diamond comes with an independent grading certificate. While the beauty of a diamond may catch your eye, its certification tells you exactly what you're purchasing. When shopping for a lab-grown diamond, you'll often come across the term IGI Certified . For many buyers, especially those purchasing online, this certificate provides reassurance that the diamond has been professionally evaluated by an independent gemological laboratory. Rather than relying solely on a retailer's description, an IGI grading report objectively documents the diamond's characteristics, including its cut, colour, clarity, carat weight, proportions, and other important details. Understanding what this report means helps you compare diamonds with confidence and ensures complete transparency before making one of life's most meaningful purchases. What Is IGI? IGI stands for the International Gemological Institute , one of the world's leading independent diamond grading laboratories. Founded in 1975, IGI has built a global reputation for evaluating both natural and lab-grown diamonds using internationally recognised grading standards. Its laboratories employ highly trained gemologists who carefully examine each diamond using specialised equipment before issuing a detailed grading report. Unlike jewellery retailers, IGI does not buy or sell diamonds. Its role is to provide an independent assessment, giving buyers confidence that the diamond they're purchasing matches its documented specifications. For lab-grown diamonds, IGI is one of the most widely recognised certification authorities in the jewellery industry. A diamond certificate isn't about increasing value—it's about increasing confidence. Why Is Diamond Certification Important? Without an independent grading report, buyers must rely entirely on the seller's description of the diamond. Certification removes much of that uncertainty by providing an unbiased evaluation performed by trained gemologists. It allows you to compare diamonds objectively rather than relying on photographs or marketing claims. Whether you're purchasing your first engagement ring or upgrading an existing piece, certification helps ensure you're receiving exactly what you've paid for. For online shoppers, this level of transparency is especially valuable because you cannot physically inspect the diamond before purchasing. Certification helps you: Verify the authenticity of the diamond. Compare diamonds fairly. Understand the quality of the stone. Confirm the 4Cs grading. Purchase with greater confidence. Receive independent documentation. Every IGI grading report contains a detailed breakdown of the diamond's characteristics. These details help buyers understand exactly what they're purchasing and make it easier to compare one diamond with another. While the layout may vary slightly depending on the report type, most IGI certificates include the same core information. An IGI certificate typically includes: Report Number Diamond Shape Cutting Style Measurements Carat Weight Colour Grade Clarity Grade Cut Grade (where applicable) Polish Symmetry Fluorescence Proportion Diagram Clarity Plot Laser Inscription (if applicable) Confirmation that the diamond is Laboratory Grown Understanding the Most Important Sections Report Number Every certified diamond receives a unique report number. This number acts as the diamond's identity and can usually be verified directly through the official IGI website. Many certified diamonds also have this report number laser-inscribed on the girdle, allowing you to match the physical diamond with its grading report. The 4Cs One of the most valuable sections of an IGI report is the grading of the 4Cs : Cut Colour Clarity Carat Weight These internationally recognised standards determine the overall quality and value of the diamond. Rather than relying on visual appearance alone, buyers can objectively compare different diamonds using these consistent grading criteria. Proportion Diagram The proportion diagram illustrates the physical dimensions and angles of the diamond. It includes measurements such as table percentage, depth percentage, crown angle, pavilion angle, and girdle thickness. Although these numbers may seem technical, they help explain how well the diamond has been cut and how effectively it reflects light. A well-proportioned diamond typically displays superior brilliance and sparkle. How to Verify an IGI Certificate One of the greatest advantages of purchasing a certified diamond is that you can independently verify the grading report before making your purchase. Every IGI certificate contains a unique report number that allows buyers to confirm the certificate's authenticity through the official IGI website. This ensures that the information provided by the jeweller matches the laboratory's records and gives you confidence that the diamond you're purchasing has been independently assessed. When buying online, verifying the certificate should become part of your buying process, just like checking customer reviews or understanding the return policy. If a jeweller cannot provide the grading report or refuses to share the report number, it is worth asking why before completing your purchase. How to verify your IGI certificate: 1. Locate the IGI report number on the certificate. 2. Visit the official IGI certificate verification page. 3. Enter the report number exactly as shown. 4. Compare the online report with the seller's listing. 5. Confirm that the shape, carat weight, colour, clarity and measurements match. 6. If available, verify the laser inscription on the diamond. Always verify before you buy. An authentic certificate should always match the diamond being sold. Many certified lab-grown diamonds feature a microscopic laser inscription on the outer edge of the diamond, known as the girdle . This inscription usually contains the diamond's unique certificate number and is invisible to the naked eye. The inscription acts like a permanent identity marker, allowing the physical diamond to be matched directly with its grading report. Jewellers use magnification tools to locate and confirm the inscription during inspections or after cleaning. Because the inscription is microscopic, it does not affect the appearance, brilliance, or durability of the diamond in any way. For buyers, it offers an additional level of confidence that the diamond and its certificate belong together. While different organisations have their own grading processes, the purpose of certification remains the same: to provide an independent assessment of a diamond's quality. For lab-grown diamonds, IGI is one of the most recognised and widely used laboratories worldwide. Many leading jewellery brands choose IGI because of its experience in grading laboratory-grown diamonds and its internationally recognised reports. Rather than focusing only on the laboratory's name, buyers should ensure the certificate is genuine, current, and issued by a respected independent organisation. When comparing certification laboratories, consider: Industry recognition. Independent grading standards. Detailed grading reports. Online verification. Global acceptance. Transparency. Common Myths About Diamond Certification There are many misconceptions surrounding certified diamonds, particularly among first-time buyers. Some people believe certification guarantees a diamond's financial value, while others assume every diamond automatically comes with a certificate. Neither assumption is correct. Certification is designed to describe the characteristics of a diamond accurately—not to determine its future resale value. Understanding what a certificate does and does not represent helps buyers make more informed decisions. Myth 1 Only expensive diamonds are certified. Reality: Many high-quality diamonds across different price ranges are independently certified. Myth 2 Certification guarantees investment value. Reality: Certification confirms quality, not future resale prices. Myth 3 Every diamond comes with a certificate. Reality: Certification depends on the jeweller and the specific diamond being sold. Myth 4 Certification and appraisal are the same thing. Reality: A grading report evaluates quality, while an appraisal estimates replacement value for insurance purposes. Tips Before Buying a Certified Diamond Before purchasing any certified diamond, take a few moments to review the grading report carefully and compare it with the product listing. A trustworthy jeweller should always be transparent about the certification, explain the report if you have questions, and provide clear information about warranties, returns, and after-sales support. Certification is an important part of the buying process, but it should be considered alongside craftsmanship, customer service, and the reputation of the retailer. Before placing your order: Read the grading report carefully. Verify the report number online. Compare the report with the product listing. Ask about laser inscription. Understand the return policy. Confirm warranty details. Buy from a trusted jeweller. Final Thoughts An independent grading report is one of the most valuable tools available to diamond buyers. It removes uncertainty, provides objective information, and allows you to compare diamonds based on internationally recognised standards rather than marketing language alone. Whether you're purchasing your first engagement ring or adding another piece to your jewellery collection, understanding how certification works gives you greater confidence throughout the buying journey. At House of Diams, every certified lab-grown diamond is selected with transparency, quality, and craftsmanship in mind. We believe informed customers make the best decisions, which is why we provide clear information about every diamond we offer. When you choose a certified diamond, you're not just investing in a beautiful piece of jewellery—you're investing in confidence, trust, and complete peace of mind. A beautiful diamond catches the eye. A trusted certificate earns your confidence. It independently identifies the stone and records information that helps you understand exactly what you're purchasing. IGI and GIA are two major gemological laboratories used for lab-grown diamonds, but their current reporting systems are not identical. This guide explains what an IGI or GIA report can tell you, how their approaches differ, what changed with GIA's lab-grown diamond assessments in 2025, how to verify a report number and laser inscription, and which details you should check before buying a certified lab-grown diamond. Lab-Grown Diamond Certification Explained: GIA vs IGI A diamond certificate is the one thing you should never buy a diamond without — natural or lab-grown. It’s an independent, third-party report confirming exactly what you’re getting: the 4Cs, the origin, and for lab-grown stones, the growth method. Here’s what the two major labs actually do differently. What a certificate actually contains Every certificate — regardless of lab — states: Carat weight, measured precisely Cut grade, from Poor to Excellent Colour grade, D through Z Clarity grade, Flawless through Included Measurements and proportions A unique report number, often laser-inscribed on the stone itself For lab-grown diamonds: explicit confirmation of lab-grown origin and growth method (CVD or HPHT) GIA (Gemological Institute of America) GIA is the oldest and most widely recognised grading lab in the world, founded in 1931. It created the 4Cs grading system that the entire industry still uses today. GIA is known for being the strictest grader — a GIA-certified stone’s grade is treated as the most conservative, trusted benchmark in the trade. GIA certificates for lab-grown diamonds are marked clearly as “Laboratory-Grown.” IGI (International Gemological Institute) IGI is the largest gemological institute by volume and has become the dominant certifier specifically for lab-grown diamonds — the majority of lab-grown stones on the market today carry an IGI report. IGI’s grading is generally considered slightly more generous than GIA’s at the same visual quality, which is worth knowing when comparing two stones with different certificates. Does it matter which one your diamond has? For lab-grown diamonds specifically, IGI is the industry standard and there’s nothing wrong with it — it’s a legitimate, widely trusted lab. The practical takeaway isn’t “GIA is better,” it’s this: when comparing two diamonds, only compare grades from the same lab. A G-colour IGI stone and a G-colour GIA stone aren’t guaranteed to look identical — GIA’s G might read closer to an IGI F in practice. If you’re comparing options, ask what each was certified by, not just the grade.
